Long-PDF Sentence Evidence — Vectorless

Build an embedding-free index of a long novel and return complete original sentences that jointly support interpretive questions.

Domain
in-document evidence retrieval
Primary focus
Index-only sentence evidence without embeddings
Primary metric
SentenceEvidenceAccuracy
vectorless evidence retrievalsearch-swe
On this page
OverviewRuntime and requirementsPublic input and output contractInputsOutputsEvaluation

Runtime and requirements

  • Agent budget: 120 minutes
  • Compute: 16 CPUs, 16 GiB RAM, 100 GiB storage; no GPU
  • Build limit: 2,400 seconds
  • Query limits: 900 seconds each; 1,800 seconds shared by the query phase
  • Concurrency: up to five queries; an additional 60 seconds allows cleanup
  • Verifier budget: 10,800 seconds

Embeddings are prohibited at every stage, including local models, endpoints and precomputed vectors. Lexical indexing, document structure and documented generation or non-embedding reranking are allowed. Only build may read the source corpus. All corpus-derived query state must be persisted inside the index directory.

Public input and output contract

Inputs

  • /task/data/corpus — the 2,043-page War and Peace PDF and sentences.jsonl, a fixed inventory of 28,798 units with sentence_id, text and pages.
  • /task/data/validation/queries.jsonl — ten public questions with query_id and query.
  • /task/data/validation/golden_answers.jsonl — support requirements and sufficient reference sentence evidence.

Twelve evaluation questions use different reference units. Physical page numbers provide provenance; they are not the scored output. Public references are examples of sufficient evidence, not the only acceptable sentence combinations.

Outputs

Submit executable scripts and dependencies under /app:

/app/build.sh --corpus /task/data/corpus --index-dir /app/index
/app/run.sh --index-dir /app/index --queries /path/to/queries.jsonl --output /path/to/results.jsonl --top-k 5

The verifier rebuilds, stops all build workers and revokes access to the PDF and sentence inventory before revealing queries. Search must run from the persisted index alone. Optional query-time services must start from that index after restart. Commands run unprivileged; public validation files are not mounted.

{"query_id":"example","results":[{"sentence_id":"inventory-id","sentence":"complete inventory text"}]}

Use exactly these fields and return zero to five distinct complete inventory units, totaling at most 16,000 sentence characters. Text must match the identified unit after NFKC and whitespace normalization. Do not add pages, scores, generated answers, paraphrases or partial sentences. Empty results are valid and score zero.

Evaluation

Evidence is judged for semantic support, not matching reference wording or sentence IDs. Equivalent explanations and harmless redundancy are accepted, while requested comparisons, qualifications and causal links must still be supported. Material contradictions or unresolved essential referents prevent complete-support credit.

The verifier checks source hashes and sentence membership. A separate answer judge evaluates whether the entire evidence set fully supports the requested interpretation. Alternative original evidence is accepted; topical similarity or the right scene alone is insufficient. SentenceEvidenceAccuracy is the fraction of all twelve questions receiving complete-support credit.

Invalid, missing, failed or timed-out queries remain in the denominator with zero, without erasing other successful queries. Shared build/setup failure prevents scoring. Judge API or parsing failures invalidate the measurement and fail closed with zero reward; they are reported separately from retrieval errors.

The answer judge is OpenRouter deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash, with high reasoning effort and temperature zero. It has a 2,700-second budget. Its credentials and model permission are not granted to submission code. A separate 3,600-second trajectory audit must return a valid binary pass to preserve the 0–1 accuracy reward.

The full contract is in the benchmark's task instructions, task documentation, and runtime configuration.
